title: Back to it
hook: don't be disgusted when you fail; return, and be glad if most of what you do is decent (Meditations 5.9)
tomorrow: How am I using my soul?

segments.voice: Yesterday: nature's prescription. Your line was the prescription. When something hard came, could you ask what it was medicine for? Day five hundred sixty-seven, the end of a week.

A knitter drops a stitch three rows back. There are two ways this can go. In one, there's a sigh, a crochet hook, the stitch is picked up, and the scarf carries on. In the other, the whole thing is yanked off the needles in disgust and shoved in a drawer for a year. The dropped stitch is the same in both. The difference is the next minute. In the ninth entry of book five, Marcus Aurelius writes to himself about exactly that minute. Today: back to it.
screen: `A DROPPED STITCH.` → `PICK IT UP, OR PULL IT ALL OUT?` → `BACK TO IT.`

segments.voice: First, don't be disgusted. Don't be disgusted, discouraged or dissatisfied, Marcus tells himself, if you don't manage to do everything by right principles. Notice that he expects to fall short. A man who wrote this much about virtue knew how often he missed it. Second, return. When you've been knocked off, he says, come back again. The whole practice is in that one word. Not never fall. Return. Third, most of it is enough. And be content, he adds, if the greater part of what you do is worthy of a human being. Not all of it. The greater part. Love the thing you're returning to. Fourth, not a schoolmaster. Then a lovely detail. Don't go back to philosophy, he says, as if to a schoolmaster with a cane, but the way people with sore eyes go back to a sponge and egg, or someone goes back to a soothing bandage or a warm compress. Philosophy, for Marcus, is the medicine, not the punishment. You return to it because it helps. And look at what this week built. Good fortune: luck is in the bearing. The gulf of time: a life against eternity. Push it away: set the troubling thought down. Fit for me: test the act, not the critics. What is mine: sincerity, dignity, endurance. The prescription: hard things as medicine. And now, back to it. You'll forget most of these lines by Thursday. That's fine. The practice was never to remember perfectly. It's to come back.
screen: `DON'T BE DISGUSTED.` · `WHEN KNOCKED OFF, RETURN.` · `CONTENT IF MOST OF IT IS DECENT.` · `A COMPRESS, NOT A SCHOOLMASTER.` · then, large: `BACK TO IT.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe. Think of one recent slip, something you meant to do or not do, and didn't manage. Notice the voice that comes with it, the disgust or the why bother. Let it speak, then let it pass. Now picture returning: the next small step back into the habit, today, as if reaching for something soothing rather than something stern. Decide what that step is. The bell holds the time.
Marcus, who told himself not to be disgusted when he fell short, but to return, and be content if the greater part was worthy. Today's word.
Your line: a sponge and egg. After your next slip, skip the speech to yourself and take the next small step back, the way you'd reach for a soothing bandage. Day five hundred sixty-seven.

howItsDone: Readers of Marcus Aurelius often use Meditations 5.9 after a lapse: no self-disgust, just a return to the practice, and contentment if most of their acts are decent.

fork.setup: you've meditated every day for two weeks, then miss three days. tonight you think: I've blown it. what fits Meditations 5.9?

sit tonight, a little, and be glad you returned.
fork.reveal: Marcus: when you've been knocked off, come back; don't return as to a stern schoolmaster, but as to a soothing remedy.

original.note: Greek, 'love of wisdom': what Marcus says to return to, as to a remedy, not a schoolmaster.

trapdoor: what you thought: don't give up.
what it means: expect to slip; skip the disgust, return, and be content if most of what you do is decent.
what a scholar hears: the 'sponge and egg' was an ordinary ancient eye remedy, so for Marcus philosophy is homely medicine.

notes: 5.9 paraphrased: be not disgusted, discouraged or dissatisfied if you do not succeed in doing everything according to right principles; when beaten back, return again, and be content if the greater part of what you do is consistent with man's nature, and love this to which you return; do not return to philosophy as to a master, but act like those with sore eyes who apply a bit of sponge and egg, or another a plaster, or a fomentation (warm compress). Confirm.
